Rashi on Ketubot 49b:10:1.hebrew: כי הא דשלח רבין באיגרתיה כו' ניסת הבת - אע"ג דאמור רבנן בעל בנכסי אשתו לוקח הוי, וקיימא לן אין מוציאין למזון האשה מנכסים משועבדים — הכא שויוהו רבנן כיורש משום פסידא דאלמנה. והכי מפורש ביש נוחלין:
Rashi on Ketubot 49b:10:1.english: Like that which Ravin sent in his letter, etc., [if] the daughter married - Even though the Sages said [that] a husband is [considered] a purchaser with respect to his wife's property, and we hold [that] one does not collect for the sustenance of a wife from encumbered property, here the Sages treated him like an heir because of the loss to the widow. And so it is explained in [the chapter] Yesh Nochalin.

Rashi on Ketubot 49b:11:1.english: The daughter died - and her husband inherits [from] her.

Rashi on Ketubot 49b:11:2.english: His widow - [The widow] of the daughter's father.

Rashi on Ketubot 49b:11:3.hebrew: ניזונת מנכסיו - ולא אמרינן, איש נכרי הוא זה, ואינו יורשו של אב אלא של אשתו, וכלוקח בעלמא דמי, ואין מוציאין למזון האשה מנכסים משועבדין:
Rashi on Ketubot 49b:11:3.english: She is sustained from his property - And we do not say [that] this [husband] is a stranger, and he is not the father's heir, rather his wife's [heir], and he is like a mere purchaser, and [therefore] we do not exact [payment] for a wife's sustenance from encumbered property.

Rashi on Ketubot 49b:11:4.hebrew: הוא ואשתו - שהוא קיים, ואלו בניו הם, ולא הוציאו מעות, אלא מתנה בעלמא:
Rashi on Ketubot 49b:11:4.english: He and his wife - For he is alive, and these are his sons, and they did not spend money, rather [it was] merely a gift.

Rashi on Ketubot 49b:11:5.hebrew: מיבעיא - ואע"ג דמתנה כמכר לענין שעבוד, התם הוא דאי לאו דעביד ליה ניחא לנפשיה לא יהיב ליה מתנה, אבל בנו ליכא למימר הכי:
Rashi on Ketubot 49b:11:5.english: Is it necessary - And even though a gift is like a sale with regard to a lien, that is [only] there, where if [the recipient] had not done something pleasing for him, he would not have given him a gift; but [with regard to] his son, one cannot say so.

Rashi on Ketubot 49b:12:1.hebrew: התם הוא דליכא דטרח קמה - שמת בעלה, להכי עבוד רבנן תקנתא:
Rashi on Ketubot 49b:12:1.english: It is there that there is no one to toil for her - For her husband died; therefore, the Sages enacted [this] ordinance.

Rashi on Ketubot 49b:12:2.hebrew: אבל הכא - דקאי איהו, נטרח לדידיה ולדידה, קמ"ל:
Rashi on Ketubot 49b:12:2.english: But here - where he is alive, he should toil for himself and for her; [therefore,] it teaches us [otherwise].

Rashi on Ketubot 49b:13:1.english: [Is] the halakha in accordance with him - [This] refers to Rabbi Ile'a.

Rashi on Ketubot 49b:13:2.english: On his foot - On his foot.

Rashi on Ketubot 49b:1:1.hebrew: דאפי' בתו - דקילא, דלא עסקא באורייתא:
Rashi on Ketubot 49b:1:1.english: That even his daughter - [who] is lesser, since she does not engage in Torah [study].

Rashi on Ketubot 49b:3:1.hebrew: ואיידי דתנא בנות כו' - לא גרסינן דתנא, דהא לא תני ליה במתני', אלא ה"ג: ואיידי דבנות לאחר מיתת אביהן חובה כו':
Rashi on Ketubot 49b:3:1.english: And since [the tanna] taught [regarding] daughters, etc. - We do not read [the word] "detana" ["it taught"], for he does not teach it in the Mishnah. Rather, this is the reading: "And since [regarding] daughters after their father's death it is an obligation, etc."

Rashi on Ketubot 49b:4:1.hebrew: באושא התקינו - כשישבו סנהדרי גזית באושא, שהיא אחת מעשר גליות שגלתה סנהדרין, כדאמר בר"ה (דף לא.):
Rashi on Ketubot 49b:4:1.english: In Usha [the Sages] instituted - When the Sanhedrin of [the Chamber of] Hewn Stone sat in Usha, which is one of the ten exiles [to which] the Sanhedrin was exiled, as is stated in Rosh Hashanah (31a).

Rashi on Ketubot 49b:4:2.english: When they are minors - Until they grow [pubic] hairs.

Rashi on Ketubot 49b:4:3.hebrew: תא שמע - דלית הלכתא כוותיה, אלא מימר אמרינן ליה ואולי יכלכלם ויזון, אבל מיכף לא כייפינן:
Rashi on Ketubot 49b:4:3.english: Come [and] hear - [This proves] that the halakha is not in accordance with his [opinion]; rather, we [merely] say [this] to him and perhaps he will support and sustain them, but we do not compel [him].

Rashi on Ketubot 49b:4:4.hebrew: יארוד - תנין. "מעון תנים" מתרגמינן "מדור יארודין" (ירמיהו ט׳:י׳), והוא אכזרי על בניו:
Rashi on Ketubot 49b:4:4.english: Yarod - A jackal [tanin]. "A den of jackals" (Jeremiah 9:10) is translated [in Aramaic as] "a dwelling of yarodin," and it is cruel toward its young.

Rashi on Ketubot 49b:4:5.english: The yarod bears [offspring] and casts [them] upon the townspeople - The crocodile [i.e., the jackal] gave birth to its young and cast their sustenance upon the townspeople.

Rashi on Ketubot 49b:5:1.hebrew: כפו ליה אסיתא - כפו מכתשת על פיה, ויעמוד זה על גב שוליה בגובה שישמעו קולו, ויכריז על עצמו שהוא רע מן העורבים, דעורבא בעי בני וההוא גברא לא בעי בני. ואית דמפרשי: שליח צבור יעמוד עליה ויאמר כן על אותו האיש:
Rashi on Ketubot 49b:5:1.english: Turn over a mortar for him - Turn a mortar upside down, and let this [man] stand on top of its bottom at a height so that [people] will hear his voice, and proclaim about himself that he is worse than the ravens, for "the raven wants [its] sons, and that man does not want [his] sons." And some explain: the communal prayer leader stands on it and says thus about that man.

Rashi on Ketubot 49b:5:2.english: To the young ravens that cry - Thus [we see that the raven] does not feed them.

Rashi on Ketubot 49b:5:3.hebrew: אוכמי - כשגדל משחיר, והאם והאב אוהבין אותן, אבל מתחילתן לבנים ושונאין אותן:
Rashi on Ketubot 49b:5:3.english: Black ones - When it grows, it turns black, and the mother and the father love them; but at the beginning [they are] white, and they hate them.

Rashi on Ketubot 49b:7:1.english: And we only said - That we do not coerce [him].

Rashi on Ketubot 49b:7:2.english: Only when he is not amid - [Meaning] that he is not wealthy.

Rashi on Ketubot 49b:7:3.hebrew: בעל כרחו - לא יהא אלא צדקה בעלמא, ואפי' אינן בניו:
Rashi on Ketubot 49b:7:3.english: Against his will - Let it be nothing more than mere charity, and even [if] they are not his children.

Rashi on Ketubot 49b:7:4.english: Like this [case] where Rava coerced him - For charity.

Rashi on Ketubot 49b:8:1.hebrew: הוא ואשתו נזונין מהן - ואפילו כתבן מעכשיו, ולא מן הדין, אלא תקנת חכמים היא:
Rashi on Ketubot 49b:8:1.english: He and his wife are sustained from them - Even if he wrote them [over] from now [effective immediately]; and [this is] not according to [strict] law, rather it is a rabbinic enactment.

Rashi on Ketubot 49b:9:1.hebrew: גדולה מזו אמרו - בגדולה מזו אמרו, כגון אלמנה ובת וניסת הבת, שאף על פי שהוא מת והנכסים נשתעבדו ללוקח דרבנן, כגון בעל בנכסי אשתו, וקי"ל (גיטין דף מח:) אין מוציאין למזון האשה מנכסים משועבדים — אפי' הכי, היכא דליכא למיחש לתיקון העולם, כגון כי האי לוקח שלא הוציא מעות, שויוהו רבנן כיורש ואמרי תזון האלמנה מנכסי בעלה:
Rashi on Ketubot 49b:9:1.english: They said a greater [ruling] than this - [That is,] they said [it] in a greater [case] than this, such as [a case of] a widow and a daughter where the daughter married; for even though he died and the property became encumbered to a rabbinic purchaser — namely, a husband with respect to his wife's property — and we hold (Gittin 48b) [that] we do not exact [payment] for a woman's sustenance from encumbered property, nevertheless, where there is no [reason] to be concerned for the betterment of the world, such as a purchaser like this who did not lay out money, the Rabbis treated him like an heir and said [that] the widow is sustained from her husband's property.

Tosafot on Ketubot 49b:4:1.hebrew: כשהם קטנים - אבל קטני קטנים, לכ"ע חייב, כדאמר בסוף אע"פ (לקמן כתובות דף סה: ושם):
Tosafot on Ketubot 49b:4:1.english: When they are minors - However, [for] very young children, according to everyone he is obligated [to sustain them], as it says at the end of [the chapter] Af Al Pi (later, Ketubot 65b, and there).

Tosafot on Ketubot 49b:5:1.hebrew: הא בחיוורי הא באוכמי - שני מיני עורבים יש: אחד לבן ואחד שחור, כדמוכח בפרק אלו טריפות (חולין דף סג.) גבי סימני עופות, דמרבה "עורב העמקי", ומפרש: "העמקי" — כמראה החמה שעמוקה מן הצל, פי': לבן:
Tosafot on Ketubot 49b:5:1.english: This [refers] to white ones, that [refers] to black ones - There are two species of ravens: one white and one black, as is evident in the chapter [entitled] Eilu Tereifot (Chullin 63a) regarding the signs of birds, where [the Gemara] includes "orev ha'amaki" [the valley raven], and explains: "ha'amaki" — like the appearance of the sun, which is deeper than the shadow; meaning, white.

Tosafot on Ketubot 49b:7:1.hebrew: אכפייה רבא כו' - וא"ת: היאך כפה אותו בשביל צדקה, והכתיב מתן שכרה בצדה, דכתיב: "(למען) יברכך", ואמרי' בפ' כל הבשר (חולין קי: ושם): כל מצות עשה שמתן שכרה בצדה, אין בית דין של מטה מוזהרין עליה? ויש לומר: דאכפייה בדברים. א"נ: קצבו ביניהן בני העיר לתת כך וכך לחדש, הלכך אכפייה, כדאמרינן בפרק קמא דבבא בתרא (דף ח: ושם): דרשאין בני העיר להסיע על קיצתן. ועוד: דבצדקה איכא תרתי לאוי — "לא תאמץ" ו"לא תקפוץ" (דברים טו):
Tosafot on Ketubot 49b:7:1.english: Rava coerced [him], etc. - And if you ask: How could he coerce him for charity, when its reward is written alongside it—as it is written, "(so that) He will bless you," and we say in the chapter Kol HaBasar (Chullin 110b and there): "Any positive commandment whose reward is [stated] alongside it, the earthly court is not charged with [enforcing] it"? One can say that he coerced him with words [alone]. Alternatively, the townspeople had fixed [an assessment] among themselves to give such-and-such per month, therefore he coerced him, as we say in the first chapter of Bava Batra (8b and there): "For the townspeople are permitted to impose penalties [for violating] their fixed agreements." And furthermore, in [the mitzvah of] charity there are two negative commandments: "you shall not harden [your heart]" and "you shall not shut [your hand]" (Deuteronomy 15).

Tosafot on Ketubot 49b:8:1.hebrew: הוא ואשתו נזונים מהם - משמע הא לאחר אין נזונין, דמתנה הויא כמכר כדפי' בקונטרס, דאי לא דעבד ליה ניחא לנפשיה לא הוה יהיב ליה, ואין מוציאין למזון האשה והבנות מנכסים משועבדים לפי שאין קצובין או לפי שאין כתובין, כדאמר בהנזקין (גיטין דף נ:). ומיהו מהכא יש לדחות, דאיכא למימר דנקט בנו משום דאיירי דנזונין אפי' ממטלטלין, אבל לאחר לא היו נזונין ממטלטלין, כמו שאין אלמנה נזונת ממטלטלין דיורשין. אי נמי משום "הוא", דאי כתב לאחר לא היה ניזון הוא, אבל היא לעולם אימא דנזונת ממתנה, אע"ג דלא טרפא מן הלקוחות. ומיהו ביש נוחלין (ב"ב דף קלג.) משמע דלא טרפא ממקבל מתנה, דקאמר: השתא ירושה דאורייתא אלמנתו ניזונת מנכסיו, מתנת שכיב מרע דרבנן לא כל שכן? משמע דממתנת בריא דאורייתא אינה ניזונת מנכסיו, אע"ג דמיתזנא מן היורשין. ואין לומר דממתנה דאורייתא נהי דכ"ש לא הוי, ה"ה מיהא הוי דלא אלים כח מתנה מכח יורשים — דעל כרחיך אלים כח מקבל מתנה מכח יורשים! דמסקינן בפ"ק דב"מ (דף יג. ושם) דשטר שיש בו אחריות נכסים לא יחזיר אפילו חייב מודה, דחיישינן לפרעון ולקנוניא, ושטר שאין בו אחריות נכסים יחזיר, דלא גבי ממשעבדי. ואי גבי ממתנה, אמאי יחזיר? אלא ודאי דלא גבי, ואילו מן היורשין גבי, דהא פסקינן בסוף גט פשוט (ב"ב דף קעו.) הלכתא: מלוה על פה גובה מן היורשין. על כן נראה דאין חילוק בין מתנה למכר לענין זה, אע"ג דיש מקומות שסברא הוא לחלק בין מתנה למכר, כמו בעשה שורו אפותיקי ומכרו (ב"ב דף מד:), דנראה דווקא מכרו, אבל נתנו — בעל חובו גובה ממנו; וכן בהנזקין (גיטין ד' נ: ושם) גבי "אין נפרעין מנכסים משועבדין במקום שיש נכסים בני חורין ואפי' הן זיבורית", מבעיא לן במתנה היאך — דווקא להא מילתא הוא דאבעיא לן, אבל הכא אין לחלק. והא דאמרינן בפ' מציאת האשה (לקמן כתובות דף סט.): "מכרו או משכנו — מוציאין לפרנסה ואין מוציאין למזונות", ה"ה נתנו. והא דנקט מכרו — לאשמועינן דאפי' במכרו מוציאין לפרנסה [ורבי חייא דמבעיא ליה במכרו או משכנו — היינו לפרנסה], אבל למזונות פשיטא ליה דאין מוציאין אפילו נתנו, כדתנן בהנזקין (גיטין דף מח:): "אין מוציאין למזון האשה והבנות מנכסים משועבדין". ולפי מה שתקנו הגאונים דאשה גובה כתובתה ומזונות ממטלטלי דיתמי, אע"ג דירושה הויא דאורייתא, כ"ש דגביא ממטלטלי דמתנת ש"מ דרבנן, דבכה"ג אמרי' ביש נוחלין (ב"ב דף קלג.). אבל מטלטלי דמתנת בריא, דהויא דאורייתא, לא גביא כתובתה; ומזונות לא גביא אפילו ממקרקעי, כי היכי דלא גביא מלקוחות, כדפרשינן. ולא מבעיא נתן הוא, אלא אפילו נתנו יתומים, אע"ג שכבר משמת נשתעבדו הנכסים:
Tosafot on Ketubot 49b:8:1.english: He and his wife are sustained from them - This implies that [if he wrote his property] to another person [who is not his son], they are not sustained [from it], for a gift is like a sale, as Rashi explained, since if [the recipient] had not done him a favor, he would not have given it to him; and one does not exact [payment] for the sustenance of a wife and daughters from encumbered property, because they are not of a fixed amount or because they are not written [in a deed], as stated in [chapter] HaNizakin (Gittin 50b). However, from here one could refute [that inference], for one could say that [the Gemara] mentioned "his son" because it is speaking [of a case] where they are sustained even from movable property, whereas [if he gave it] to another person they would not be sustained from movable property, just as a widow is not sustained from the movable property of heirs. Alternatively, [it mentioned his sons] because of "he" [himself] — for if he wrote [his property] to another person, he [himself] would not be sustained, but as for her [i.e., his wife], I could still say that she is sustained from a gift, even though she does not collect from purchasers. However, in [chapter] Yesh Nochalin (Bava Batra 133a) it is implied that she does not collect from the recipient of a gift, for [the Gemara] says: "Now, [if in the case of] inheritance, which is biblical, his widow is sustained from his property, [then in the case of] a gift of a deathly ill person, which is rabbinic, is it not all the more so?" This implies that from a gift of a healthy person, which is biblical, she is not sustained from his property, even though she is sustained from the heirs. And one cannot say that from a biblical gift, granted it is not an "all the more so," nevertheless it is the same [as inheritance], for the power of a gift is no stronger than the power of heirs — because perforce the power of a gift recipient is stronger than the power of heirs! For we conclude in the first chapter of Bava Metzia (13a and there) that a promissory note containing a property lien should not be returned [to the lender] even if the debtor admits [it is unpaid], because we are concerned about [prior] payment and collusion, whereas a note that does not contain a property lien should be returned, because [the lender] does not collect from encumbered property. Now, if he collected from a gift, why should it be returned? Rather, it is certain that he does not collect [from a gift], whereas from heirs he does collect, as we rule at the end of [chapter] Get Pashut (Bava Batra 176a) that the law is that an oral loan is collected from heirs. Therefore, it appears that there is no distinction between a gift and a sale in this matter, even though there are places where it is logical to distinguish between a gift and a sale — such as [the case where] one made his ox an apotiki [designated security] and sold it (Bava Batra 44b), where it appears that specifically if he sold it [the creditor cannot collect], whereas if he gave it as a gift, his creditor collects from it; and similarly in [chapter] HaNizakin (Gittin 50b and there) regarding "one does not exact [payment] from encumbered property where there is unencumbered property, even if it is of inferior quality," where we ask what the law is regarding a gift — [nevertheless,] it is specifically regarding that matter that we asked, but here we do not distinguish. And that which we say in the chapter Metziat HaIshah (below, Ketubot 69a): "If he sold them or pledged them, one exacts [payment] for [the daughter's] dowry, but one does not exact [payment] for sustenance," the same applies if he gave them as a gift. And the reason it mentioned "sold them" is to teach us that even if he sold them one exacts [payment] for dowry [and Rabbi Chiya, who asked regarding "sold them or pledged them," was referring to dowry], whereas for sustenance it was obvious to him that one does not exact [payment] even if he gave them as a gift, as we learned in the Mishnah in [chapter] HaNizakin (Gittin 48b): "One does not exact [payment] for the sustenance of a wife and daughters from encumbered property." And according to what the Geonim instituted, that a woman collects her ketubah and sustenance from the movable property of orphans, even though inheritance is biblical, all the more so does she collect from the movable property of a gift of a deathly ill person, which is rabbinic, for in this manner we say in [chapter] Yesh Nochalin (Bava Batra 133a). However, from the movable property of a gift of a healthy person, which is biblical, she does not collect her ketubah; and sustenance she does not collect even from real property, just as she does not collect from purchasers, as we have explained. And not only [if] he [the husband] gave [it away], but even if the orphans gave [it away], even though the property had already become encumbered upon his death:

Tosafot on Ketubot 49b:9:1.hebrew: אלמנתו נזונת מנכסיו הוא ואשתו מבעיא - אע"ג דלא דמי, דהתם אינן יכולין לירש אלא מה שהוא מוריש, ומזון אלמנה הוא חייב מקודם — מכל מקום מייתי הכי: הואיל ואלמוה רבנן לשעבודא דידה, שאף מן הבעל, שאינו כיורש אלא כלוקח, גובה, אע"ג דלא היתה גובה מלוקח אחר — הכי נמי אית לן לתקוני בכותב לבנו, שיהא הוא ואשתו נזונין מהן:
Tosafot on Ketubot 49b:9:1.english: "His widow is sustained from his property; is [there a] need [to state this regarding] him and his wife?" - Even though [the two cases] are not comparable — for there, [the heirs] can only inherit what he leaves behind, and he was already obligated for [his] widow's sustenance beforehand — nevertheless, [the Gemara] cites [it] thus: since the Rabbis strengthened her lien so that she collects even from the husband [of a daughter who inherited], who is not like an heir but rather like a purchaser, even though she would not collect from another purchaser, so too we ought to enact regarding one who writes [his property] to his son that he and his wife should be sustained from them [the gifted properties].
